title: Illumina Metabarcoding Protocol for Fungi in Marine Sediments
author: Lluvia Vargas-Gastélum
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yupfwvn

Once all samples are measured, repeat step 3.

steps.title: Prepare Sterile Syringes
steps.instruction: Prepare syringes for sampling while maintaining sterility near a gas burner.

substeps.instruction: Keep a microcentrifuge tube containing 1 mL of sterile HPLC grade water open near the working area (Control #1).
Attach a new scalpel blade to the handle and flame sterilize it using a gas burner.
Open a sterile syringe package by the end where the tip is located, avoiding the plunger.
Carefully cut and remove the syringe tip.
Close the syringe package and secure it with adhesive tape.
Sterilize the scalpel again before cutting any additional tips.

steps.title: Prepare Sucrose Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare and sterilize the sucrose buffer solution.

substeps.instruction: Keep an open microcentrifuge tube containing 1 mL of sterile HPLC grade water during preparation (Control #2).
Mix reagents for 100 mL of sucrose buffer: shake vigorously, add distilled water up to 80 mL, adjust pH to 9, and fill to a final volume of 100 mL with distilled water.
Near a gas burner, place a 0.2 µm pore filter in a syringe and filter the buffer, collecting the sterile solution in 50 mL tubes.
Keep a microcentrifuge tube with 1 mL of sterile sucrose buffer open near the gas burner once prepared (Control #3).

steps.title: Collect Sediment Samples
steps.instruction: Collect sediment cores and preserve them in sucrose buffer.

substeps.instruction: Label tubes with station number, date, depth, and sub-sampling number.
Keep an open microcentrifuge tube of 1 mL sterile HPLC grade water (Control #4) and 1 mL sterile sucrose buffer (Control #5) during sample preparation.
Make a reference mark on the core to split it into two halves.
Open five pre-cut 10 mL syringes and pull back the plungers.
Immerse syringe cylinders into one half of the core to take the sample.
Push the plunger to dispense the first 5 mL (10 cm depth) into a 15 mL screw cap tube, and the remaining 5 mL (first 5 cm) into another 15 mL screw cap tube.
Pipette 5 mL of sterile sucrose buffer into each 15 mL tube (final concentration 25% w/v).
Shake tubes to homogenize buffer and sediment.
Seal tubes with screw caps, wrap with parafilm, and store in Ziploc® bags at -20°C during transport.

steps.title: Sample Processing and Lyophilization
steps.instruction: Remove preservation buffer and dry the samples.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge samples at maximum velocity for 1 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant (sucrose buffer).
Store samples at -80°C or keep in sucrose buffer at -20°C until processing.
Place uncapped tubes on ice and cover the tops with parafilm.
Use a sterile needle to make holes in the parafilm.
Lyophilize and check after 48 hours by shaking to ensure sediment is totally dry.
Cap tubes and store at -80°C.

steps.title: DNA Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract DNA using a modified PowerSoil kit protocol.

substeps.instruction: Prepare PCR chamber: clean glass walls, place materials inside, close, and turn on UV light for 15 min; then turn on white light and air circulator.
Keep a microcentrifuge tube containing 1 mL of sterile HPLC grade water open (Control #6).
Weigh 0.15 g of lyophilized sample into a PowerBead tube. (If not lyophilized, remove 100 µL of PowerBead solution first).
Add 60 µL of C1 solution.
Add 100 µL of phenol chloroform in a chemical fume hood and incubate for 2 min at room temperature.
Lay samples horizontally in a vortex adapter and vortex for 30 seconds.
Centrifuge for 1 min and transfer the supernatant to a sterile 2 mL tube.
Add 250 µL of C2 solution, vortex for 5 seconds, and incubate on ice for 5 min.
Centrifuge for 2 min and transfer 600 µL of supernatant to a sterile 2 mL tube.
Add 200 µL of C3 solution, vortex for 5 seconds, and incubate on ice for 5 min.
Centrifuge for 3 min and transfer up to 850 µL of supernatant to a sterile 2 mL tube.
Add 650 µL of C4 solution and 450 µL of absolute ethanol, then vortex for 5 seconds.
Load up to 500 µL onto a column tube, centrifuge for 30 seconds, and discard flow through; repeat until the sample is processed.
Centrifuge for 2 min and transfer the column to a new sterile 2 mL tube.
Add 600 µL of absolute ethanol, centrifuge for 30 seconds, and discard flow through.
Centrifuge for 3 min and discard flow through.
Add 650 µL of C5 solution, centrifuge for 30 seconds, and discard flow through.
Centrifuge for 4 min and transfer the column to a new sterile 2 mL tube.
Add 50 µL of C6 solution, incubate at room temperature for 15 min, and centrifuge for 1.5 min.
Add another 50 µL of C6 solution, incubate at room temperature for 15 min, and centrifuge for 2 min.

steps.title: DNA Quality and Quantity Assessment
steps.instruction: Verify DNA extraction using electrophoresis, NanoDrop, and Qubit.

substeps.instruction: Run electrophoresis on a 1% agarose gel using 5 µL of DNA per sample.

NanoDrop: Select DNA > dsDNA. Clean pedestals with 2 µL sterile HPLC grade water, wait 2 min, and wipe with Kimwipes. Establish a blank with 1 µL blank solution. Measure 1 µL of sample (mixing with pipette). Repeat 2-3 times.
Qubit: Dilute Qubit BR Reagent (A) 1:200 in Qubit BR buffer (B) to make working solution (final volume 200 µL per tube).
Prepare Standard 1 (0 ng/µL) and Standard 2 (10 ng/µL) by adding 10 µL standard to 190 µL working solution.
Prepare samples by adding 3 µL DNA to 197 µL working solution.
Vortex samples/standards (2-3 secs), spin briefly, and incubate at room temperature for 2 min.
Use Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer (dsDNA High Sensitivity assay) to read standards and then samples (3 µL volume, ng/µL units).

steps.title: First PCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Amplify the ITS1 region of rDNA.

substeps.instruction: Prepare PCR chamber (clean, UV 15 min, white light/air circulator).
Adjust genomic DNA concentration to 2 ng/µL and keep on ice.
Prepare master mix using ITS1F and ITS2 primers (plus sequencing primer) and reagents from Table 2, adding 10% extra volume.
Include Controls 1-6, a negative control (sterile HPLC grade H2O), and a positive control (mock community).
Perform Touchdown PCR (program in Figure 3-B).
Run 5 µL of product on a 2% agarose gel to check for fragments >300 bp.

steps.title: PCR Purification
steps.instruction: Remove primer-dimers (~120 bp) using the Just-a-Plate™ 96 PCR Purification Kit.

substeps.instruction: Prepare PCR chamber (clean, UV 15 min, white light/air circulator).
If first use: add 96 mL of 100% ethanol to Washing Buffer II (WB2) and mix.
Mix 100 µL Binding Buffer (KB5) and 400 µL Isopropanol (IPP) in a 1.5 mL tube; invert 10 times.
Add 37 µL of this working Binding Buffer to 45 µL of PCR product in 8 wells; mix by pipetting up and down 10 times.
Cover plate with adhesive cover and spin for 10 min at 2250 x g at room temperature.
Remove cover, flip plate over a waste container, and shake briskly to remove solution.
Add 150 µL Washing Buffer II to each well, pipet up/down 2 times, wait 30 secs, and remove solution by flipping/shaking.
Repeat the wash step (Step 8-9) once more, then repeat the flip/shake (Step 8).
Blot dry the inverted plate on absorbent paper 3-4 times.
Add 20 µL elution buffer to each well, cover, vortex for 30 secs, and spin for 30 secs.
Verify by loading 5 µL into a 1% agarose gel.

steps.title: Second PCR and Sequencing Preparation
steps.instruction: Attach Illumina adapters and barcodes for sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Assign combinations of i7 (12 available) and i5 (8 available) indexes for up to 96 samples.
Prepare master mix using reagents from Table 3 and perform PCR (program in Figure 2-C).
Visualize products on a 2% agarose gel (load 5 µL); expect sizes from 300 bp to 800-900 bp.
Normalize samples using the SequalPrep™ Normalization Plate Kit per supplier instructions.
Sequence using MiSeq Reagent Kit v3 (600-cycle) to obtain 300 bp for forward and reverse ends.
